Similar through-joins: Account#featured_in_collections (api/v1/in_collections_controller.rb:32), Account#curated_collection_items (block_service.rb:34).

sql: DELETE FROM collection_items WHERE collection_items.collection_id = 1 AND collection_items.uri NOT IN ('x', 'y')
notes: NOT IN over a non-empty list is never true for NULL uri, so the delete only touches rows with uri IS NOT NULL (an empty list gives NOT (1=0) and also deletes NULL-uri rows). Anti-membership, not a point query.

sql: SELECT collection_items.* FROM collection_items INNER JOIN accounts ON accounts.id = collection_items.account_id WHERE collection_items.collection_id = 1 AND accounts.domain IS NULL AND collection_items.state = 1 AND collection_items.uri IS NULL AND collection_items.account_id = 2 ORDER BY collection_items.id ASC LIMIT 1

sql: SELECT coalesce(nullif(accounts.shared_inbox_url, ''), accounts.inbox_url) AS preferred_inbox_url FROM accounts INNER JOIN collection_items ON accounts.id = collection_items.account_id WHERE collection_items.collection_id = 1 AND collection_items.state IN (0, 1) AND accounts.protocol = 1 GROUP BY preferred_inbox_url
notes: Through-association join on account_id, not uri. Same for featured_in_collections (in_collections_controller.rb:32) and curated_collection_items (block_service.rb:34).

sql: SELECT conversations.* FROM conversations WHERE conversations.uri = 'x' LIMIT 1

notes: Raw SQL (maintenance.rb:791). GROUP BY on the key with the predicate written out; HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 is empty under the index. The CLI drops the index first (line 424), so the index is absent when this runs.

No app code queries refresh_token.

notes: Correlated on in_reply_to_id (line 224: reblog_of_id), not uri. notes: Upsert arbitrating on the partial index.

sql: DELETE FROM tagged_objects WHERE tagged_objects.status_id = 1 AND tagged_objects.uri NOT IN ('x', 'y')

sql: SELECT tagged_objects.* FROM tagged_objects WHERE tagged_objects.status_id IN (1, 2, 3)
notes: Preload on the key prefix status_id only.

sql: SELECT 1 AS one FROM merchants WHERE merchants.type = 'FamilyMerchant' AND merchants.name = 'x' AND merchants.family_id = 'uuid-1' LIMIT 1
notes: STI subclass FamilyMerchant: the validator's finder_class.unscoped keeps the STI type condition, which is exactly the index predicate. On update AND merchants.id != 'uuid-2' is added.

sql: SELECT merchants.name FROM merchants WHERE merchants.type = 'FamilyMerchant' AND merchants.family_id = 'uuid-1'
notes: has_many :merchants, class_name: 'FamilyMerchant' (family.rb:31) adds the STI type condition, so this scans the index-key prefix with the predicate; the names are distinct per family. Similar: set_transaction_merchant.rb:7, auto_merchant_detector.rb:73.

sql: SELECT transactions.* FROM transactions INNER JOIN entries ON transactions.id = entries.entryable_id INNER JOIN accounts ON entries.account_id = accounts.id INNER JOIN merchants ON merchants.id = transactions.merchant_id WHERE accounts.family_id = 'uuid-1' AND entries.entryable_type = 'Transaction' AND merchants.name IN ('x')
notes: Transaction belongs_to :merchant targets the base class Merchant, so there is no type condition. The join is on merchants.id (PK), and only name is filtered: the key (family_id, name) is not equated and the type predicate is absent.

sql: SELECT transactions.* FROM transactions LEFT OUTER JOIN merchants ON merchants.id = transactions.merchant_id WHERE merchants.id = 'uuid-2'
notes: Join on PK, base class Merchant, no type condition. The filter comes from apply() via build_sanitized_where_condition. api/v1/transactions_controller.rb:246 has the same left_joins(:merchant) with a merchants.name ILIKE filter.

sql: SELECT merchants.* FROM merchants WHERE merchants.type = 'ProviderMerchant' AND merchants.source = 'plaid' AND merchants.name = 'x' LIMIT 1
notes: The STI type condition equals the index predicate, and the full key is equated.

sql: SELECT merchants.* FROM merchants WHERE merchants.type = 'ProviderMerchant' AND merchants.source = 'ai' AND merchants.name = 'x' AND merchants.website_url = 'https://x' LIMIT 1
notes: Full key plus predicate, with an extra website_url filter. A website_url mismatch causes an INSERT that then violates the unique index.

sql: SELECT 1 AS one FROM merchants WHERE merchants.type = 'ProviderMerchant' AND merchants.name = 'x' AND merchants.source = 'plaid' LIMIT 1
notes: STI type condition retained in the uniqueness validator.

sql: SELECT transactions.* FROM transactions INNER JOIN entries ON transactions.id = entries.entryable_id INNER JOIN accounts ON entries.account_id = accounts.id INNER JOIN merchants ON merchants.id = transactions.merchant_id WHERE accounts.family_id = 'uuid-1' AND entries.entryable_type = 'Transaction' AND merchants.name IN ('x')
notes: Join on PK through the base class Merchant (no type condition). Also left_joins(:merchant) at rule/condition_filter/transaction_merchant.rb:11 and api/v1/transactions_controller.rb:246.

otp_secret is only written (user.rb:126/141) and read as an attribute on an already-loaded user (user.rb:148/154/191, mfa_controller.rb:7). No query filters, joins, groups or validates on it. Users are only fetched by id, email or token_for.
